article_title: First 100% British chocolate bar since 1932 made in Reading

tasks.prompt: What is the main focus of the article?
options: A British company has stopped importing all cocoa
A university student made a chocolate bar entirely from British ingredients, illustrating both the work behind chocolate and global supply challenges
Princess Elizabeth opened a chocolate factory in Reading
British farmers now grow most of the world's cocoa
tasks.correct_answer: A university student made a chocolate bar entirely from British ingredients, illustrating both the work behind chocolate and global supply challenges
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת בחטיף שוקולד שיוצר כולו מחומרי גלם בריטיים, ובאמצעותו מסבירה את תהליך הייצור ואת פגיעוּת שרשרת האספקה.

tasks.prompt: Why was the bar named the “Reading 100 Chocolate Bar”?
options: It contains exactly 100 cocoa beans
It took 100 days to make
It marks the University of Reading's 100th anniversary
It is the hundredth chocolate recipe made in Britain
tasks.correct_answer: It marks the University of Reading's 100th anniversary
tasks.explanation_hebrew: השם מציין מאה שנים לאוניברסיטת רדינג, שחוגגת את יום השנה המאה שלה ב־2026.

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does “reliant on imported cocoa” mean?
options: Able to produce cocoa without farms
Unwilling to sell cocoa abroad
Protected from changes in world trade
Dependent on cocoa brought in from other countries
tasks.correct_answer: Dependent on cocoa brought in from other countries
tasks.explanation_hebrew: reliant on פירושו תלוי ב־; תעשיית השוקולד הבריטית תלויה בקקאו שמיובא ממדינות אחרות.

tasks.prompt: Where was the cocoa for the new bar grown?
options: At the University of Reading's International Cocoa Quarantine Centre in Berkshire
On a commercial plantation in Brazil
At Rowntree's former factory in York
In a greenhouse owned by Princess Elizabeth
tasks.correct_answer: At the University of Reading's International Cocoa Quarantine Centre in Berkshire
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הקקאו גדל במרכז ההסגר הבינלאומי לקקאו של אוניברסיטת רדינג שבברקשייר.

tasks.prompt: Why does the quarantine centre carefully control the movement of cocoa plants?
options: To make every cocoa bean taste identical
To prevent pests and diseases spreading between cocoa-growing regions
To stop students from seeing the plants
To ensure that all chocolate is made in Britain
tasks.correct_answer: To prevent pests and diseases spreading between cocoa-growing regions
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הבקרה וההסגר נועדו למנוע העברה של מזיקים ומחלות מאזור גידול אחד לאחר.

tasks.prompt: What does “resilient” mean when the article calls for a resilient global cocoa market?
options: Able to recover and continue despite difficulties
Made only from local ingredients
Certain to remain cheap forever
Closed to international farmers
tasks.correct_answer: Able to recover and continue despite difficulties
tasks.explanation_hebrew: resilient מתאר מערכת שיכולה להתמודד עם משברים ולהמשיך לפעול או להתאושש מהם.

tasks.prompt: Name three steps used to turn the Reading cocoa pods into a finished chocolate bar.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שלושה שלבים מדויקים מתהליך הייצור המתואר בכתבה.
expected_points: The pods were opened and the beans removed
The beans were fermented and dried
The beans were roasted, crushed and ground into cocoa powder
The cocoa was mixed with British sugar and milk
The mixture was heated, shaped and formed into a bar

tasks.prompt: Summarise why the Reading chocolate bar is historically interesting and what wider issue it highlights.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול את הייחוד ההיסטורי, הקשר ליום השנה של האוניברסיטה, ותלות תעשיית השוקולד בסחר ובחקלאים בעולם.
expected_points: It is thought to be the first bar made from British-grown cocoa since 1932
It was created for the University of Reading's centenary
Britain's large chocolate market normally depends entirely on imported cocoa
The project highlights climate risks and the importance of protecting cocoa varieties and farmers

tasks.prompt: Why does the article say that buying local food is not always a universal solution?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שלגידול מקומי יש יתרונות, אך גידולים טרופיים וסחר בינלאומי תומכים גם בחקלאים, ביעילות הייצור וביציבות כלכלית.
expected_points: Some crops naturally grow better in climates outside Britain
International food trade supports smallholder farmers and communities
Natural energy and suitable climates can make overseas production sensible
A resilient supply chain needs research and protected crop varieties, not only local production

tasks.prompt: Using the article, explain two ways research can make the future cocoa supply more secure.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע שתי דרכים ולהסביר כיצד כל אחת מסייעת מול שינוי אקלים, מזיקים או מחלות.
expected_points: Maintain diverse cocoa varieties so harder plants are available
Use quarantine controls to prevent pests and diseases spreading
Study cocoa plants under controlled conditions
Support farmers and global supply chains exposed to climate risks
